newsitem.title: THAILAND: Electricity Generating venture gets loan.
newsitem.headline: Electricity Generating venture gets loan.

text.p: A joint venture firm of Electricity Generating Plc, Amata-EGCO Power Ltd, secured 3.4 billion baht in short-term and long-term loans for its power plant under construction, Amata-Egco said on Friday.
The company said it had received a 14-year loan of approximately 2.5 billion baht (US$100 million) from KfW of Germany and another 900 million baht in short- and long-term loans from Bangkok Bank.
The company did not reveal the terms governing the loans.
Amata-EGCO Power is a joint venture between Amata power and the Electricity Generating Plc, the company said in a statement.
The venture was set up to develop and operate a combined cycle power plant now under construction at Bangpakong Industrial Park on the outskirts of Bangkok.

The construction of first phase of the power plant is expected to be completed in early 1998 with a capacity of 160 MW. But the plant will start distributing electricity by mid-1997, the company said.
The company planned to expand the production capacity to 350 MW to serve the increasing demand in the industrial park, it added.
